lesson.meaning: To keep something going or to provide support for it over a period of time.
examples: It's important to eat healthy food to sustain your energy throughout the day.
Our team needs to sustain this high level of productivity to meet the project deadline.
During the meeting, we discussed how to sustain customer satisfaction even after the new update.
To sustain a successful career, continuous learning and adaptation are essential.
The company's new policy aims to sustain a positive work-life balance for all employees.
lesson.memory_tip: Think of 'sustain' as giving something the power to 'stay' and 'continue' for a long time!
